sentences.Det er typisk norsk å spise hvalkjøtt, s: It's typically Norwegian to eat whale meat, Pablo says to Haifa.
sentences.Andre vil si at det er typisk norsk å sp: Others would say it's typically Norwegian to eat waffles, drink lots of milk or go hiking in all kinds of weather.
sentences.Her forteller Ebow Annan fra Ghana hva h: Here Ebow Annan from Ghana tells us what he thinks is typically Norwegian:
sentences.Jeg heter Ebow Annan, er 24 år gammel og: My name is Ebow Annan, I'm 24 years old and I'm from Ghana.
I have lived in Norway for four years.
sentences.For tre år siden møtte jeg en hyggelig,: Three years ago I met a nice Norwegian family, and they invited me on a trip to their cabin in the mountains.
sentences.Jeg ble veldig glad og tok på meg pene k: I was very happy and put on nice clothes and shoes.
sentences.Vi gikk i en halv time fra parkeringspla: We walked for half an hour from the car park to the cabin.
sentences.Det var ikke vei til hytta, og skoene mi: There was no road to the cabin, and my shoes got wet and dirty.
sentences.Den var lita og hadde ikke strøm eller v: It was small and had no electricity or running water.
sentences.Familien hentet vann fra ei elv i nærhet: The family fetched water from a river nearby.
But that wasn't the worst part.
sentences.Hytta hadde ikke WC, men et lite hus, en: The cabin had no toilet, just a little hut, an "outhouse", ten metres from the cabin.
sentences.Det luktet ikke godt der!: It didn't smell nice in there!
sentences.Familien var ganske rik, men de elsket h: The family was quite rich, but they loved their cabin and often went there.
sentences.I dag vet jeg at mange norske hytter har: Today I know that many Norwegian cabins have electricity and water, but I still think "my" family is typically Norwegian.
sentences.De liker at hytta er lita og primitiv og: They like their cabin to be small and primitive and far away from other people.
I think that's a bit strange.
